title: Sleeping Area
preview: On the second floor, the windmill becomes intimate. This was not only a working building, but also a place where the miller's family rested beside the stored wheat and flour.
details: Please watch your step on the wooden stairs and mind the low timber above you. The windmill was built for work first, so every movement inside it asks for attention.

On one side, historic images show windmills from across Greece. On the other, the room recalls a more personal truth: the miller and his family slept close to the sound, movement and responsibility of the mill.

items.label: Stored wheat
items.text: Bags of raw wheat and fresh flour stayed nearby because flour meant food, income and security.

items.label: Shared space
items.text: Rest, storage and responsibility had to fit inside the same small working building.

items.label: Family life
items.text: The room shows how private life and labor could meet closely in an island household.

details: Continue upward to the machinery, where the wooden structure and stone wheels reveal how wind became flour.

items.text: Where would you put a pillow?
